title: performance_rating is approximately normally distributed
summary: Shapiro-Wilk test (W=0.9947, p=0.0071) rejects normality at alpha=0.05. The histogram shows a bell-shaped distribution centered near 50 with std ~10.

title: No numeric feature is significantly correlated with performance_rating after correction
summary: After Bonferroni correction, 0 of 7 features reject H0. After BH correction, 0 reject. All bootstrap 95% CIs for Pearson r mostly include zero.

title: salary_band shows no significant effect on performance_rating
summary: One-way ANOVA F=0.7185, p=0.5794. Not significant at alpha=0.05. Box plots show overlapping distributions across all salary bands.

title: OLS model has no predictive power beyond the mean baseline
summary: OLS R²=0.01359, global F-test p=0.4564. Cross-validated RMSE (10.06) is within 1% of the baseline RMSE (10.01).

title: No feature has meaningful permutation importance
summary: Random-forest permutation importance shows all features with 95% CIs overlapping zero or near-zero values. RF cross-validated RMSE (10.45) is similar to baseline (10.01).

title: Predictor variables are mutually uncorrelated
summary: Maximum VIF across predictors is 1.013 (threshold <2). Condition number is 28.83. The correlation heatmap shows no strong pairwise relationships.

title: Dataset is confirmed pure noise with no exploitable signal
summary: Across all analyses — correlation tests, ANOVA, OLS regression, random-forest permutation importance, and multiple-testing corrections — no statistically significant relationship was found between any feature and performance_rating. This is consistent with the dataset being entirely synthetically generated noise.
